title: What Was Left Behind
logline: Weeks after a grandfather's funeral, his family finally opens the room he never let anyone into, and has to decide what a half-finished life becomes now.

object.note: Object 8 (identity not chosen) could enter only if the family willingly offers something that belonged to the person who is gone. Never staged, and never implied to be 'meant' to be found.

thread_in.thread: The body ends, so what carries on? Weeks after a funeral, a family opens the room of someone who is gone and faces what a half-finished life becomes.

thread_out.thread: What is left behind leads to what the living still do: a family cooking through the night for a seventh-day almsgiving, pouring water until it overflows.

requirements: A household that has recently lost an elder and is willing to be filmed sorting belongings
A room or set of rooms not yet cleared since a death
Enough trust for the family to speak plainly about any disagreements

suggestions.name: A hill-country village in the Kandy or Matale district
suggestions.why: A common house form with an elder's room set apart; suggested for texture and access, not for a specific household.
suggestions.verify: No specific household identified; region-level suggestion only.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed.

lesson.in_simple_terms: When someone dies, much of what they set in motion is still unfinished, and some of it will never come due at all. The texts also say that nothing of the person crosses into a next life: what carries on is a chain of causes, not a traveller.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: කෙනෙකු මිය යන විට ඔවුන් පටන් ගත් බොහෝ දේ තවමත් නිම නොවී පවතින නමුත්, ඊළඟ ජීවිතයට ඔවුන්ගෙන් කිසිවක් රැගෙන නොයන බවත්, ඉදිරියට යන්නේ හේතු ඵල දාමයක් පමණක් බවත් ධර්මය කියයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma sorts intentional action (kamma) by when its result ripens: in this life, in the next, in some later life whenever an opening comes, or never, when it lapses. The Pradeepika compares action that loses its chance to seed grain kept past its season, which will not sprout. On rebirth, both sources say that nothing mental or physical passes from one existence to the next; the new life arises fresh, as the result of what went before.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Drawers open one by one on a life caught in the middle of things: letters, an old ledger, a repair left half done, an extension never finished. As the family decides out loud what to finish, sell or let go, the viewer feels for themselves that a life does not close its accounts neatly. When one object is carried out 'because it was his', the film leaves that instinct beside the teaching that nothing of him travels on, without resolving it.

key_terms.en: lapsed action; action that never ripens
rebirth-linking consciousness, the first mind of a new life
the continuum or stream of mind

lesson.caution: Lapsed action is not forgiveness or a clean slate, and the things a family keeps are not the person living on: in the texts, what continues is a stream of mind, not a legacy or a memory.
lesson.builds_on: The previous group ended with a body that must end and asked what carries on; this film gives the first answer, that a life stops unfinished and what continues is a chain of causes, not a traveller.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
